goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `<%- end if %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:4 is a Ruby syntax error so the template never compiles, causing 500 errors on /embed/best requests with a topic_id
The specs never catch the template syntax error because both success tests stub TopicView.new to return nil and never actually render the view

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the “success” examples exercise the controller action but do not render the views (typical RSpec controller specs unless `render_views` is enabled), so ERB/template syntax issues in `app/views/embed/*` would not be caught. Additionally, the second success test sets an expectation on `TopicView.new` without specifying a return value (`TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)`), which in Mocha will return `nil` by default—further indicating the view isn’t being meaningfully exercised. (The finding overstates slightly: the first success test doesn’t stub `TopicView.new`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-49 asserts an execution path the controller does not have: the controller calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) not TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve, so the mocha expectation fails

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb#best`, when `topic_id` is nil the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)` and renders `loading`; it never calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` ("tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found") sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)...` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, which will not be satisfied by the actual controller code, causing the spec to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The after block's response.should be_success fails because the un-stubbed enqueued job path never sets @topic_view

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and explicitly `render 'loading'` (which does not reference `@topic_view` at all), so the response can still be successful without setting `@topic_view`. The spec’s `after` block asserting `response.should be_success` is not invalid for that path based on the diff; the finding misattributes a failure to the “enqueued job path never sets @topic_view.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: The following test's TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5}) returns nil, so the view crashes on @topic_view.posts

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` sets an expectation but does not affect real application behavior; in production `TopicView.new(...)` returns a `TopicView` object, not `nil`. Also, this controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so the ERB view code (`@topic_view.posts`) is not executed during the test and cannot “crash” due to `@topic_view` being `nil` from the mock setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 `i.content.scrub` crashes with NoMethodError on plain RSS 2.0 feeds because SimpleRSS only defines content for Atom entries and RSS 2.0 items carry description
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that calling `i.content.scrub` can raise a NoMethodError because `i.content` is often nil on RSS 2.0 feeds (which use `description` instead). This matches the golden issue and implies the same need for a fallback to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The poll_feed job has retry: false, so the first failing item on an RSS feed kills the job and no topics are ever imported

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `sidekiq_options retry: false` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, but the claim that “the first failing item on an RSS feed kills the job and no topics are ever imported” is not supported. While an exception anywhere in `poll_feed` (including within `rss.items.each`) would abort that run, `retry: false` only disables Sidekiq retry; this is a scheduled job (`recurrence { hourly }`) and would run again later. Also, earlier items in the loop could have been imported before a failure. The “no topics are ever imported” conclusion overstates behavior not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The primary Gemfile.lock is missing ruby-readability, simple-rss, and guess_html_encoding (only Gemfile_rails4.lock was regenerated), causing bundle install --deployment failures and LoadError on require

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile` and updates only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` to include those gems (and `guess_html_encoding`). There is no change shown to any primary `Gemfile.lock`, so if the project expects a non-rails4 lockfile to be kept in sync, this PR leaves it outdated. The claimed bundle/deployment failure depends on repository conventions not visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` raises NoMethodError on nil when embed_by_username is unset, crashing retrieve_topic jobs on every embed request from the host

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http the code calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` before any nil/blank guard. If `embed_by_username` is unset (nil), this will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no preceding check in `retrieve`/`perform_retrieve` to ensure `embed_by_username` is present; only `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` checks it, but `TopicRetriever` can reach `fetch_http` independently (e.g., embed requests when feed polling is disabled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41-42 runs the entire feed poll synchronously via Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inside the retrieve_topic worker thread, blocking a sidekiq worker for the duration of a full feed import

adjudication.rationale: Verified in lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve`: when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, not via `Jobs.enqueue`. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (a Sidekiq job) invokes `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, so the Sidekiq worker thread can be occupied while `PollFeed#poll_feed` performs network I/O (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports items. This is a real architecture/performance concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js ships inert: it has no precompile registration and no route serves it, so third-party sites cannot load the embed script in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, but nothing in the shown views/layouts references it (the new `embed` layout only includes `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` and inline JS). The diff also doesn’t show any asset manifest / precompile-list change to ensure `embed.js` is compiled for production. So it’s a concrete integration gap (potentially making the script unavailable/unused), though the claim that “no route serves it” isn’t verifiable from this diff alone since Rails assets are typically served under `/assets` rather than via explicit routes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: View closes first conditional with `<%- end if %>`, generating Ruby with bare `end if` statement causing SyntaxError and 500 on every /embed/best request
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same ERB/Ruby syntax bug: the template uses `<%- end if %>` to close an `if` block, which produces invalid Ruby (`end if`) and causes a render-time SyntaxError; it should be just `end`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New retrieve_topic job logic (invalid-parameter raise and staff no_throttle bypass) has zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new job `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb) with nontrivial logic: it raises `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `args[:embed_url]` is missing and conditionally sets `no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)` when calling `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`. In the added specs, there are tests for `TopicRetriever`, `EmbedController`, `PollFeed`, and `TopicEmbed`, but no spec file covers `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so this new behavior has no direct test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration change to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` drops existing top_topics table in production, destroying TopTopic data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the migration `CreateTopTopics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb). In Rails, `force: true` will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, which can cause data loss if this migration is ever executed against an existing `top_topics` table. However, in normal production `db:migrate` flow, an already-run migration is not re-executed (tracked in `schema_migrations`), so the finding's “on re-run in production” scenario is conditional rather than a guaranteed defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported feed content stored with cook_method: raw_html and rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`; poll_feed path uses scrubbed content with no tag filtering, allowing arbitrary HTML/script injection from a compromised feed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a raw-HTML rendering path for imported content: `Post#cook` returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html`. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, feed item content is only `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (no sanitization/allowlist), then passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw` (confirmed by the new spec). This combination allows arbitrary HTML/script from a compromised feed to be stored and executed (XSS) when the embed page is viewed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading page reloads every 30s but retrieval throttled to 60s and silently no-ops on failure, causing infinite spinner with no error state or spec for failed retrieval

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loading view that unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), while retrieval is throttled to once per 60s in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? via Redis setnx/expire (lib/topic_retriever.rb). When no TopicEmbed exists, the controller always enqueues a retrieve job and renders the loading page (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), but there is no explicit error state if retrieval cannot succeed (e.g., TopicRetriever#fetch_http returns early if embed_by_username user is missing, or import_remote/open fails and no embed is created). This is a concrete UX/robustness gap created by the change (potentially long/indefinite loading with no feedback) and lacks test coverage for failure paths, but it’s not a strictly provable “defect” because eventual success depends on external conditions and the throttle only delays retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed executed synchronously inside perform_retrieve; feed fetch/parse exceptions kill the retrieve with no retry and embed never appears

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (not enqueued). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `SimpleRSS.parse` with no exception handling. Any network/parse exception will bubble up and abort `perform_retrieve` before it can reach `fetch_http`, so the embed retrieval can fail entirely when feed polling is enabled but the feed is temporarily broken/unreachable. (The finding’s “no retry” rationale is a bit off—`retry: false` only applies if PollFeed runs via Sidekiq—but the unhandled exception blocking retrieval is verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key (SHA1 of polling URL) is dead code, never referenced, misleading future maintainers and losing conditional-GET caching

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `Jobs::PollFeed` class, the `feed_key` method (building a Redis key from SHA1 of `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff. `poll_feed` always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates items without using `feed_key` (or any conditional-GET / last-modified caching), so the method is dead/misleading code as the finding states. This is a maintainability/scope issue rather than a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import rewritten to TopicEmbed.import_remote drops created_at and category, so imported topics get current timestamps instead of original dates

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the previous `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` call (and `--category` option handling) was removed and replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` only pass `title`, `raw` (content), and `cook_method` to `PostCreator` and do not set `created_at` or category anywhere in the new code, so imported topics/posts will use current timestamps and no longer honor the original Disqus thread date or chosen category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed update path does `post = embed.post` with no nil check; deleted post causes NoMethodError in retry:false PollFeed job, killing the whole feed poll loop

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path (`else` when an existing `TopicEmbed` is found) does `post = embed.post` and then may call `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!` if `content_sha1` changed, with no guard for `post` being `nil` (e.g., if the associated post was deleted but the `topic_embeds` row remains). That would raise (at least) a `NoMethodError` inside `PostRevisor`/`revise!`, and `Jobs::PollFeed` iterates items without rescue (`rss.items.each`), so one exception would abort the whole polling run. The job is `retry: false`, so it would not be retried automatically.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController has no handling for topic_id whose topic is deleted or restricted; TopicView.new raises or leaks restricted topics to anonymous iframe viewers, unverified by stubbed specs

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a `topic_id`, the code blindly does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no check that the topic still exists or is viewable (no rescue/guard around `TopicView.new`). The added controller spec only stubs `topic_id_for_embed` and asserts `TopicView.new` is called, so it doesn’t cover cases like deleted topics or permission-denied topics. However, the diff doesn’t show `TopicView`’s internals, so whether this actually leaks restricted topics can’t be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls port handling is scheme-blind (adds any non-80/443 port regardless of scheme), and protocol-relative URLs in RSS content are left broken; spec only covers default-port case

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix appends `:#{uri.port}` only when the port is not 80 and not 443, without considering the URL scheme (`http` vs `https`). This will incorrectly omit the port for valid non-default combinations like `http://host:443/...` or `https://host:80/...` (diff: `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`). Also, protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x` satisfy `start_with?('/')` and get rewritten as if they were path-relative, producing an incorrect URL under the source host rather than preserving the external host. The included spec only tests a default-port, path-relative case and wouldn’t catch these failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js origin check uses substring indexOf match, so unrelated origins containing the discourse URL substring pass the check and can drive iframe.height
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: origin validation uses indexOf/substring matching, allowing a malicious origin that merely contains the trusted domain string (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com) to bypass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding `force: true` to existing migration `create_top_topics.rb` is untraceable to PR intent and could drop the table in environments that replay migrations

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an already-existing migration (`db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, so re-running that migration (e.g., via manual migration replay/partial reruns) could cause data loss in `top_topics`. This risk is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import task's `--category`/`-c` CLI option is silently removed, deleting existing operator capability to choose a category

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the Disqus Thor task’s `--category`/`-c` option (`method_option :category` deleted) and deletes the corresponding `category_id` resolution and passing `category: category_id` into `PostCreator`. The task now always imports via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` with no category selection, so operator capability to choose a category is removed (a breaking CLI/behavior change), though it may be intentional rather than an outright defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import is rewired through `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, coupling it to embed settings and failing when `embeddable_host` doesn't match Disqus permalink hosts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does rewire Disqus import to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` (in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`). However, `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not reference `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` or enforce host matching; the only host check against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, which is used by the embed retrieval job/controller path, not by the Disqus import task. So the claimed failure mode (“failing when embeddable_host doesn't match Disqus permalink hosts”) is not supported by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `PostCreator` no longer passes `category_id`, a regression for existing task users

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the `:category` CLI option is removed and the previous logic that resolved `category_id` and passed `category: category_id` into `PostCreator.new(...)` is deleted. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`, and `TopicEmbed.import` constructs `PostCreator.new(...)` without any category parameter. This is a verifiable regression for users of the disqus import task who relied on specifying a target category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `raw_html` cook method returns `raw` before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook)`, bypassing plugin cook pipeline for imported posts (security-relevant)

adjudication.rationale: In `Post#cook`, the new early return (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`) happens before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so `:after_post_cook` plugins will not run for `raw_html` posts (e.g., those created via `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change and could matter for plugins (potentially including security-related transformations), but the diff comment indicates this bypass is intentional and the diff alone doesn’t prove it is an actual vulnerability/defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js placed in `app/assets/javascripts/` asset pipeline is dead code shipped in every instance's application.js instead of a standalone distributable

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new asset file `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, but it does not show any manifest change (e.g., `application.js` `//= require embed` or `require_tree`) that would cause it to be bundled into every instance’s `application.js`. The claim that it is “dead code” and “shipped in every instance's application.js” is not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New locale key `embed.permalink` has zero consumers (dead surface)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `embed.permalink` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`, but no code in the added embed views (`app/views/embed/*.erb`), layout, JS, or other changed files references `t('embed.permalink')`/`I18n.t('embed.permalink')`. This makes the new locale entry appear unused (dead surface), which is a maintainability/cleanup issue rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `EmbedController` passes `embed_url` unvalidated to the job, enqueuing Sidekiq jobs for invalid input since format validation only occurs deeper in `TopicEmbed.import`

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` is enqueued into `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` without validating it is a well-formed URL or that its host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (the controller only validates the *referer* host in `ensure_embeddable`). Invalid or wrong-host `embed_url` values would still generate Sidekiq jobs, even though `TopicRetriever#retrieve` later short-circuits via `invalid_host?` (URI parse / host check). The finding’s claim that validation “only occurs deeper in `TopicEmbed.import`” is not accurate (there is earlier validation in `TopicRetriever`), but the diff does show unnecessary job enqueues for bad `embed_url` inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Write path and lookup path store/compare embed_url in different canonical forms with no normalization (no strip, downcase, or trailing-slash trim), so the embed never resolves and the page reloads every 30 seconds forever

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows lookup and storage both use the exact `embed_url` string without any transformation: `EmbedController#best` calls `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which does `where(embed_url: embed_url)`, and the write paths (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote/import`) persist `embed_url: url` where `url` is the same value passed through from `args[:embed_url]` / `@embed_url`. There is no evidence of “different canonical forms” between read and write that would prevent resolution and cause perpetual reloads. While lack of normalization could theoretically cause duplicates for semantically-equivalent URLs, that’s not what the finding claims and isn’t verifiable as an infinite-reload defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic synchronously re-runs the entire feed poll inline (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute) plus a page fetch — two unbounded network calls with no timeout, stalling the retrieve job

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, the retrieve path can synchronously invoke `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, and if that doesn’t create the embed it then calls `fetch_http`, which does `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` and ultimately `open(url).read` (and `PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`). This is all performed inline within the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job (which just calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`), so the job runtime is directly coupled to external network fetches and potentially a full feed scan. However, the claim of “no timeout” being truly unbounded isn’t strictly verifiable from the diff alone because `open-uri` has implicit defaults, even though no explicit timeouts are set here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key method in poll_feed.rb:21-23 is defined but never called, so the implied feed-modified throttle does not exist and the two import entry points share no throttling

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` (lines ~21-23) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff; `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all items each run. That makes the “feed-modified” key/throttle implied by `feed_key` effectively nonexistent (dead code / incomplete feature). However, this isn’t a correctness defect by itself because `TopicEmbed.import` dedupes/updates via `embed_url` uniqueness and `content_sha1`, so repeated polling mostly causes extra work rather than broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS content imported via TopicEmbed.import is stored as raw_html completely unsanitized (no whitelist, unlike import_remote's Readability path), allowing script/iframe injection from a malicious feed rendered on the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `Jobs::PollFeed` parses feed items and passes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly into `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization/whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` and explicitly bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so any `<script>`, `<iframe>`, event handlers, etc. from a malicious RSS/Atom feed would be served and executed on the Discourse origin inside the embed iframe. This contrasts with `import_remote`, which uses ruby-readability with explicit tag/attribute allowlists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path in topic_embed.rb:28-30 crashes with NoMethodError when the referenced post has been deleted (PostRevisor.new(nil)), and because PollFeed has retry: false, one deleted post permanently wedges the entire feed pipeline

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then, if the SHA changed, unconditionally does `PostRevisor.new(post)` (topic_embed.rb ~lines 28-30 in the diff). If the referenced Post row has been deleted, `embed.post` will be nil and this will raise (likely NoMethodError inside PostRevisor). Jobs::PollFeed is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single such exception will cause that feed polling run to fail and it will keep failing on subsequent scheduled runs until the bad embed record is cleaned up, effectively wedging the pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer/host comparison in embed_controller.rb:24-27 compares the referer host against raw free-text SiteSetting.embeddable_host with no case normalization, causing valid embed requests to be rejected with 403

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the check `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` does a case-sensitive string comparison with no normalization (e.g., `downcase`). Since hostnames are case-insensitive and `URI(...).host` may preserve the referer’s original casing, valid requests can be incorrectly rejected when `embeddable_host` and the referer host differ only by case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method is set via a bare untyped integer from Post.cook_methods passed through PostCreator's generic @opts hash with no validation, so a typo'd value silently falls through to the normal cooking pipeline producing corrupted output

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `cook_method` as an integer column (`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`) and sets it in `PostCreator` via the generic `@opts` hash (`post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method] if @opts[:cook_method].present?`) without validating that the value is one of `Post.cook_methods` (an `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`). In `Post#cook`, only the exact `raw_html` enum value short-circuits; any other/invalid integer will fall back to the normal cooking pipeline. This is a concrete robustness/validation gap grounded in the diff, but the diff itself passes a correct value (`Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `TopicEmbed.import`), so it’s not a verifiable introduced defect unless/until callers pass bad values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with no error state when RetrieveTopic no-ops (e.g. embed_by_username unset or host mismatch), bouncing visitors with no cap or operator signal

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`, the page unconditionally reloads every 30 seconds (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)`), with no cap or error/timeout UI. In `EmbedController#best`, when no topic is found it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. But `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early if `embed_by_username` doesn’t resolve to a user (`return if user.blank?`), and `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can also no-op if `invalid_host?` is true. In these cases no `TopicEmbed` is ever created, so subsequent reloads keep re-enqueuing/looping indefinitely with no operator signal or stop condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race on embed_url: where(...).first followed by TopicEmbed.create! can raise on concurrent writers, and with PollFeed's retry: false this aborts remaining feed items for that run

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later does `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. The migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`, so concurrent callers importing the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then one will raise on the unique constraint during `create!` (classic TOCTOU). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without rescuing, so an exception from `TopicEmbed.import` would abort the job mid-run, skipping remaining feed items; `sidekiq_options retry: false` makes that loss for that run more likely to persist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration file 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb modified to add force: true, which will destructively drop existing top_topics table and data on already-migrated deployments; shipped migrations should be immutable

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which is generally discouraged because released migrations are expected to be immutable. However, the finding’s specific data-loss claim for "already-migrated deployments" isn’t directly verifiable from the diff: Rails won’t re-run a migration that’s already recorded as applied, so the destructive drop would only occur if the migration were re-executed (e.g., during resets/rollbacks), not during normal upgrades.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import command removed the --category/-c option, category_id lookup, and created_at parsing, breaking existing operator scripts and silently changing import semantics with no replacement or deprecation

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the diff removes `method_option :category` (and the associated `category_id` lookup) and stops passing `created_at`/`category` into `PostCreator` (replacing the whole creation path with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`). This is a clear, diff-verifiable change to the Disqus import CLI interface and import semantics (no category routing, no created_at parsing), which could break existing invocations, but it’s a backward-compatibility/behavior-change concern rather than an objectively incorrect implementation per the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook short-circuits raw_html before applying the after_post_cook plugin filter, silently skipping documented plugin filters for raw_html posts

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/post.rb`, `cook` now returns early for `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (`return raw if ...`) before the call to `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. This verifiably changes behavior so the `:after_post_cook` plugin filter is not applied to `raw_html` posts. The diff doesn’t show any requirement that plugins must still run for this mode, so it’s not clearly a correctness bug, but it is a concrete compatibility/extension concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PostRevisor's save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations]) creates a general-purpose validation bypass reachable by any revise! caller rather than scoping it to TopicEmbed's use

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, meaning any caller of `revise!(..., opts)` can now bypass validations by passing `skip_validations: true` (as `TopicEmbed.import` does). This is a broad API/architecture change introduced in `lib/post_revisor.rb`, not scoped to embedding-specific code, and could enable saving invalid posts if misused elsewhere, but it is not a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS via raw_html cook method: Post#cook returns raw verbatim and TopicEmbed.import stores unsanitized third-party RSS content (Jobs::PollFeed) rendered with raw on /embed/best

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `raw` derived from third-party content (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`; `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` + `Readability::Document#content`). No sanitization is applied before storing/rendering. The embed view renders `post.cooked` with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML/JS in the feed/article content will be persisted and served, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: https?:// prefix check on url in TopicEmbed.import doesn't prevent single-quote breakout in the injected <a href='#{url}'> imported_from footer

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML footer containing `#{url}` directly into `contents` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (no HTML escaping). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, this HTML is rendered as-is, and the embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. A `url` containing a literal single quote (`'`) can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and inject arbitrary attributes/HTML, so the prefix check does not prevent the single-quote breakout described in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Readability tag/attribute allowlist in import_remote doesn't sanitize URI schemes, allowing javascript: hrefs and onerror attributes in stored raw_html content

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, remote HTML is processed via `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: ..., attributes: %w[href src])` and then imported with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see `TopicEmbed.import`), which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` and `embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The diff shows no additional sanitization step for allowed `href`/`src` values (e.g., blocking `javascript:` URIs), so a malicious/compromised embedded host could inject dangerous schemes into stored/displayed HTML. The finding’s mention of `onerror` is not supported by the diff because only `href`/`src` are allowlisted, but the URI-scheme issue is a verifiable security defect given the raw_html bypass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses substring origin check (indexOf) instead of equality for postMessage origin validation

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the postMessage handler validates origin with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`. This is a substring/prefix containment check rather than comparing normalized origins (e.g., `e.origin === expectedOrigin`). That makes the origin validation weaker/brittle and can potentially accept messages from unintended origins if `discourseUrl` contains `e.origin` as a substring, instead of requiring an exact match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed layout interpolates client-supplied request.referer into inline JS as postMessage targetOrigin instead of a server-known constant
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root problem: the code uses the full referrer URL (from request.referer, client-supplied) as postMessage’s targetOrigin, rather than a proper origin value (scheme+host+port). This can cause postMessage to be dropped and break resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec failure-path tests assert only response.should_not be_success, which cannot distinguish intended 403 (Discourse::InvalidAccess) from accidental 500 or NoMethodError crashes

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the failure-path examples ("is 404 without an embed_url", "raises an error with a missing host", "raises an error with no referer") only assert `response.should_not be_success`. They do not assert a specific status code (e.g., 403/404) or that `Discourse::InvalidAccess` is raised, so these tests would also pass on unintended 500s/NoMethodError crashes. This is a concrete test-precision gap introduced with the new controller/spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed spec only tests the settings gate; the new poll_feed logic (i.link blank fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML content scrub, TopicEmbed.import) has zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the tests only cover `execute` gating and that it delegates to `poll_feed` (e.g., `poller.expects(:poll_feed).once`). There are no specs exercising `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` itself, which contains new nontrivial behavior: `url = i.link; url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)`. That logic (including fallback URL selection and content handling) has zero direct coverage in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever_spec stubs perform_retrieve and retrieved_recently?, so TopicRetriever's body (Redis setnx/expire throttle, early-return, PollFeed invocation, no_throttle staff path) is never executed

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false and only set expectations on `perform_retrieve` (once/never) rather than executing it. As a result, none of TopicRetriever’s substantive logic is exercised in this spec: the Redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?` (`$redis.setnx`/`expire`), the early-return checks inside `perform_retrieve` (`TopicEmbed.where(...).exists?`), the `Jobs::PollFeed` invocation when `feed_polling_enabled?`, and the `no_throttle` path. This is a concrete test-coverage gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:15 contains a broken ERB terminator <%- end if %>, a syntax error that would cause /embed/best to 500 in production, and no test renders the template

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the header block ends with `<%- end if %>`, which would generate Ruby `end if` after an `if/else` block (`<%- if ... %> ... <%- else %> ...`), an invalid Ruby construct and thus a template syntax error. That would cause `/embed/best` to error when the template is actually rendered. The controller spec does not enable `render_views`, so it would not catch this template syntax error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed_spec update-path test only asserts cooked content changed, leaving the content_sha1 change-detection branch unverified (no test for unchanged content causing no revision, or sha1 being updated)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path explicitly gates revisions on `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and updates the stored SHA via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. The spec’s update test (`"Supports updating the post"`) only asserts that the returned post’s `cooked` includes the new contents after calling `TopicEmbed.import` again; it does not assert that `topic_embeds.content_sha1` is updated, nor does it cover the no-op branch where the SHA is unchanged (ensuring no revision occurs). This leaves the change-detection logic effectively unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in Jobs::PollFeed is dead code with no caller and no test references, creating a comprehension hazard

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `Jobs::PollFeed` defines `def feed_key` (building a Redis key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`), but the diff shows no usage of `feed_key` within `PollFeed` (the job uses `poll_feed`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, and iterates items) and no other added/modified code references it. The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` also does not mention `feed_key`. This makes `feed_key` dead/unused code introduced by the diff, which can confuse readers/maintainers even if it doesn’t break behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec retriever test verifies the mock invocation but never checks Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic) arguments, so swapped or nil arguments would pass

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the no-topic path enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`'s "tells the topic retriever to work" example mocks `TopicRetriever.new`/`retriever.retrieve` and does not assert anything about the `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` call or its arguments, so the enqueue payload (e.g., wrong/missing `embed_url`/`user_id`) is untested by that spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to already-shipped migration CreateTopTopics makes replayed migrations silently DROP TABLE top_topics, destroying aggregation data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. If this migration is ever executed against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., inconsistent schema_migrations state, manual rerun), it will silently DROP the table and lose aggregation data instead of failing safely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :topic_embeds with force: true on new table silently drops data if migration is ever replayed in an environment with existing data

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb` creates the table with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can silently destroy existing `topic_embeds` data if the migration is re-run (e.g., in certain rebuild/replay/rollback+redo scenarios).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed update path assumes embed.post exists; if post/topic was deleted (no dependent: :destroy or FK cascade), PostRevisor.new(nil) crashes the PollFeed job, permanently wedging feed polling due to retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import's update path, it does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally (when sha differs) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revise!` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Since the migration creates topic_embeds without any FK constraint and the model has no `dependent: :destroy` linkage, it is possible for a topic_embeds row to remain while the referenced Post/Topic is deleted, making `embed.post` nil and causing a crash. This failure can propagate from Jobs::PollFeed (sidekiq_options retry: false), so an exception would cause the scheduled run to fail and keep failing on subsequent schedules until data is cleaned up.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 is computed over raw contents but post stores absolutize_urls output, so changed absolutization produces identical sha1 and skips revision, leaving stale/incorrectly-absolutized links

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, `content_sha1` is computed from `contents` (after appending the "Imported from" footer) before applying `absolutize_urls`, but the post’s stored `raw` (and thus `cooked` for `raw_html`) is the result of `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`. The update path only revises the post when `content_sha1` changes, so if the absolutization/serialization logic changes (e.g., different `absolutize_urls` behavior or Nokogiri HTML normalization differences) while the source `contents` remains identical, the SHA won’t change and the post won’t be revised, potentially leaving stale/non-canonical links. This is a diff-grounded correctness risk/design issue, but it’s not a directly verifiable runtime defect solely from this diff because `absolutize_urls` is deterministic for a given `url`+`contents` in the current code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill/import path uses skip_validations and interpolates unescaped #{url} into the 'imported from' HTML footer, allowing malformed/injected HTML persisted as cooked and rendered via raw

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import` appends an HTML footer that interpolates `url` directly into an `#{url}` string (no escaping/sanitization) and only guards it with a loose `^https?://` regex, which would still allow quotes/attribute injection in the URL. The post is then created with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`; the embed view renders via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes the injected/malformed HTML persist and be rendered, i.e., a stored XSS/vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle key committed before fetch operation succeeds with non-atomic setnx/expire, so a crash between them leaves the key with no TTL and permanently throttles the embed_url, causing infinite loading screen

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `retrieved_recently?` throttles by doing `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands and are not atomic; if the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without a TTL, causing permanent throttling for that `embed_url`. Since `EmbedController#best` enqueues retrieval and renders `loading` when no topic exists, a permanently-throttled URL can keep the system from ever fetching/creating the embed, resulting in repeated loading page reloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle key set before fetch_http runs means a failure in import_remote (unguarded open(url).read) still spends the 60-second throttle and subsequent requests silently no-op while the topic is never created

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, `retrieved_recently?` is called before `perform_retrieve` and sets the Redis throttle key (`$redis.setnx` + `expire` for 60s) on the first attempt. If `perform_retrieve` then fails (e.g., `fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` with no rescue), the job/request can error out but the throttle key remains, causing subsequent calls within 60 seconds to return early (`retrieve` skips `perform_retrieve` when `retrieved_recently?` is true). This matches the finding: a failed import still consumes the throttle window and delays topic creation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: content_sha1 updated via update_column unconditionally after revise! without checking its return value, so a failed or skipped revision is permanently masked as 'unchanged content' and the post never updates

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `content_sha1` differs it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` regardless of whether the revision actually happened or succeeded. The diff shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` early (`return false if not should_revise?`), and `update_post` now does `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` without checking success. Because `update_column` bypasses validations/callbacks and is unconditional here, a failed/skipped revision can still advance `content_sha1`, preventing future updates for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: revise! returning false on unchanged content vs. a failed save is indistinguishable in the update path

adjudication.rationale: In the new embed update path (TopicEmbed.import), PostRevisor#revise! is only called when content_sha1 differs (so it’s not the “unchanged content” case), and the caller ignores revise!’s return value entirely. While revise! can return false when should_revise? is false, the diff doesn’t show revise!’s full return semantics on save failure vs. no-op, nor any code that depends on distinguishing those cases. The finding isn’t directly verifiable or actionable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed has retry: false and no per-item error handling, so one malformed feed item (nil content, missing id/link, title failure) aborts the entire poll, silently dropping subsequent items with no retry or logging

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and then iterates `rss.items.each` without any per-item rescue. Inside the loop it does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, which will raise if `i.content` is nil/non-string, aborting the entire poll and preventing subsequent items from being processed in that run. With retries disabled, Sidekiq will not automatically retry the job, so a consistently malformed item can repeatedly prevent later items from importing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A persistently bad feed item permanently wedges polling at that point in the feed since retries are disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed`, `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set and the job does not rescue per-item failures. Any exception while fetching/parsing the feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) or processing an item (`i.content.scrub`, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import`) will abort the whole job, preventing later items from being processed. If the feed consistently contains a bad/edge-case item, each hourly run will fail at that point and effectively block progress past it (with no Sidekiq retry to recover within the same run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: nil embed.post (deleted post/trashed topic with surviving topic_embeds row) crashes the update path with PostRevisor.new(nil) NoMethodError, with no destroy-dependency or nil guard on the association

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally constructs `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changes. If the `topic_embeds` row exists but the associated `post` has been deleted (no `dependent:` option shown on `belongs_to :post`, and no DB foreign key/cascade in the migration), `embed.post` can be `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` inside `PostRevisor` when it dereferences `@post` (e.g., `@post.acting_user = ...`). There is no nil guard or cleanup for this orphaned-association case in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare open-uri fetches (feed polling URL and import_remote's open(url).read) have no connect/read timeout, so a slow or hung host blocks the Sidekiq worker indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces network fetches using `open-uri` without any timeout configuration: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). In Sidekiq-executed code paths (`Jobs::PollFeed` and `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `import_remote`), a slow/hung remote host can block the worker thread for an unbounded time because no connect/read timeouts are set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Feed/article fetches have no read-length limit, so a hostile or huge body is read fully into memory on request-triggered paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces unbounded network reads into memory on attacker-influenced URLs. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (lib/topic_embed.rb) with no size/read limit, and `Jobs::PollFeed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) likewise. These paths can be triggered via `EmbedController#best` enqueueing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with a user-supplied `embed_url` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb, app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb, lib/topic_retriever.rb), allowing a hostile or huge response body to be fully read into memory (DoS risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: RetrieveTopic synchronously re-polls the entire RSS feed inline (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute) on every uncached embed hit, causing N sequential remote fetches per page, with the per-embed_url throttle not bounding the shared feed fetch

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `perform_retrieve` explicitly runs the feed poller inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` then does a remote fetch via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. The only throttling shown (`retrieved_recently?`) is keyed to `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`, so it limits repeated work per *embed_url* but does not bound repeated full-feed fetches across many different uncached embed URLs. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the diff, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading view reloads forever every 30 seconds with no retry cap or failure state, giving the embed consumer an eternal spinner when retrieval fails or is throttled

adjudication.rationale: The new loading template unconditionally calls `document.location.reload()` every 30000ms with no attempt counter or error UI (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`). In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` returns nil it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders this loading view, but the diff shows no failure handling if retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., remote fetch errors, invalid content, persistent throttling/invalid host). This can lead to an indefinite reload loop / “eternal spinner” UX, though it’s not a strictly incorrect program state per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is not normalized before lookup, so trailing slashes, case changes, or query params create duplicate topic_embeds rows and duplicate topics for the same logical article

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up TopicEmbed records by the raw embed URL string with no canonicalization: `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import` and `topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does an exact `where(embed_url: embed_url)`. The DB uniqueness is also only on the raw `embed_url` string (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). Therefore URL variants (trailing slash differences, case changes, or differing query params) will not match existing rows and can create additional TopicEmbed rows and new topics for the same logical article.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing embed_url param raises ActionController::ParameterMissing mapped to a 500 instead of the promised 4xx (Discourse::InvalidParameters 400)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the code uses `params.require(:embed_url)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` when absent, and there’s no local rescue/translation to `Discourse::InvalidParameters` like the job (`RetrieveTopic`) does. The diff alone does not prove this becomes an HTTP 500 (Rails often maps `ParameterMissing` to 400), nor does it show a “promised” 400 via `Discourse::InvalidParameters`, but it does show inconsistent error handling for the missing param case.
